She did not know how long Xiao Huaiyan's feelings would last.

The heart of an emperor was so difficult to read. Who could say when it would change?

He wanted only her at this moment. But what of later?

If something changed, could she bear it?

"Your Majesty." Jiang Mi called to him softly.

He answered, and waited.

She gathered her courage and looked up at him. "Your Majesty — will you give me an imperial edict? If you fail to keep your word, the edict should release me from the palace and leave me free from any interference in my life — including in my marriage. Will you agree?"

At the words marriage and free, Xiao Huaiyan's eyelid gave a twitch. A vein appeared faintly at his temple.

Before he could speak, Jiang Mi sniffed.

"I want an edict sealed with the imperial seal — not one used to deceive me." Tears began to fall. She still remembered — the engagement promise he had made once before, when he had agreed with his mouth and never issued the edict.

Xiao Huaiyan went rigid. He looked at her aggrieved expression, reached out to wipe her tears, and said, "I will seal it. I will give it to you. I am not deceiving you."

She was still crying and still uncertain, even as he said it. He added, "I promise you — you will have that edict."

Jiang Mi blinked. She had not expected him to agree so quickly.

Xiao Huaiyan pressed a light kiss to her lips. "Now that I have given you this edict — will you agree to enter the palace?"

Jiang Mi nodded without a sound. Since there was no escape, she would face it.

Xiao Huaiyan wanted very much to smile, but Jiang Mi's eyes were still red and her feelings not yet settled.

He was afraid that if he showed too much happiness, she would want to take it back.

He pressed his feelings down and gathered her into his arms.

Warm and soft in his embrace, he said, "I will go back and seal the edict tonight. I will have it sent to you before the night is out. Wait calmly."

Jiang Mi was already growing sleepy. She nodded in a haze.

......

The next morning, Jiang Mi woke and rubbed her head on the pillow.

She looked at her loosened inner garments, found her silk stockings had gone missing as well, and felt a low ache in her back.

She did not dare call Qiuyu in.

She put on a thin outer robe and sat at her dressing table. She looked at the red marks at her neck and collarbone and felt a surge of vexation.

She would have to wear a crossed-collar dress to cover them.

She had a quiet breakfast in the Yuanzhǐ Courtyard and played with Mianmian and the kittens for a while.

Then Qiuyu came in. "Miss — I just heard from the first branch that the Third Master is to return to the capital. It seems he has been doing very well in his post, and the Emperor has summoned him back."

Jiang Mi stood up. "Third Uncle is coming back? Then Second Cousin and Fifth Sister will be returning too."

Qiuyu nodded. "Yes, Miss. The house will be livelier then." She caught herself, thinking of the First Master's demotion and impending departure for Yizhou.

Then Xiàruò came running back across the courtyard, face bright, gasping for breath. "Miss — wonderful news! The Master has been promoted!"

Jiang Mi was taken aback. "Father has been promoted?"

Xiàruò nodded emphatically. "The Master has been raised to Assistant Minister of the Board of Works. They say he distinguished himself in some matter — the Emperor was greatly pleased and gave him the post."

Jiang Mi sat back down slowly.

She was beginning to understand.

The Jiang family was a whole. With her great-uncle demoted, the other two branches would need to hold the household up.

Her Third Uncle's and her father's promotions were Xiao Huaiyan's way of preparing the ground for the investiture. But it felt very fast.

She wondered whether it would draw censure from the censors and remonstrance officials.

Once the Empress investiture edict was proclaimed, the Jiang family would be placed directly over a fire.

In the early afternoon, Li Fu came to see her.

All her maids had been sent away. Li Fu carried a rosewood box and bowed with great respect. "Your Highness — this is the edict His Majesty asked this servant to deliver."

Jiang Mi felt a small jolt at Li Fu's form of address.

"Thank you, Eunuch Li. Please do not address me so."

Li Fu bent at the waist with a smile. "Your Highness must not embarrass this servant. This is what is right. And besides — addressing Your Highness thus is only a matter of time."

Jiang Mi felt the shift in his manner. She said nothing more.

When Li Fu had gone, Jiang Mi opened the rosewood box and took out the edict. She looked immediately for the imperial seal.

She read it carefully from start to finish. Nothing had been omitted. Everything she had asked for was there.

She sat holding it, a strange feeling of unreality moving through her.

......

In the first days of the sixth month, the entire Jiang household was absorbed in preparations for Jiang Yì's wedding.

Then an imperial edict naming the Empress shook the entire court.

For so long the Emperor had named neither Empress nor consort — and now, when he finally acted, the edict he issued named the eldest daughter of Jiang Qingxuān, Assistant Minister of the Board of Works, as Empress.

And not a single consort was named alongside her.

Many in the court had not yet absorbed it. Some looked toward Grand Secretary Shen. Others exchanged glances. Some watched the Minister of War and the Loyal and Brave Marquess.

Grand Secretary Shen's expression showed a faint change. The Minister of War and the Loyal and Brave Marquess remained composed.

Before long, a censor by the name of Lín stepped forward with a direct remonstrance against the choice of Empress.

This Jiang girl had previously been engaged to the Duke Zhenguo's heir, and her great-uncle, the former Marquess of Cheng'en, had broken the law and been demoted to a distant post. She was entirely unsuitable as Empress.

This censor had barely finished speaking when Pei Chi, who rarely spoke in court, came forward and filed a counter-memorial.

Pei Chi then enumerated how this particular censor had redeemed a woman from a pleasure house as a kept mistress, and how the money used to redeem her had come from crooked sources. He listed in turn the times and places where the censor had accepted bribes and abused his position. Then he submitted a ledger.

The censor broke out in a cold sweat and loudly proclaimed his innocence.

Xiao Huaiyan did not look at the ledger. He handed the matter to the Board of Punishments for investigation, and the censor was hauled out by the Embroidered Guard.

He smiled. "This is my domestic matter. Do any other ministers have objections?"

The civil and military officials, whatever they thought privately, all understood. Not a word more was ventured. Their voices rose in unison: "We congratulate Your Majesty on this great joy."

Even the officials of the Board of Rites who had been considering raising the matter of additional consorts for the purpose of heirs did not dare bring it up at this moment.

Jiang Qingxuān walked out of the court feeling as though his feet were floating on air. His face ached from smiling.

He had never dreamed, in any dream, that the Emperor would name Tangtan as Empress.

The news of the investiture reached the Ci'ning Palace quickly.

The Empress Dowager was so startled she knocked the medicine bowl from her own hands.

Since the Jiang family's wrongdoing had been exposed, the Empress Dowager had been carefully keeping herself small and as unobtrusive as possible. She had not directly harmed Consort Jin — but the Jiang family's fault remained. And so she had not dared take the slightest issue with the Emperor's handling of the Jiang family's case.

She had only meant to take good care of herself and hold on a little longer for the family's sake.

She had never dared to dream that the new Empress would come from the Jiang family again.

chapters.title: Chapter 103
chapters.content:
From inside the Changchun Palace, the sound of shattering porcelain came at intervals.

The palace attendants were too frightened to make a sound.

Princess An'yang swept everything from the table in a fury — the teacups all smashed to the floor.

Still not satisfied, she pulled a whip from the wall and lashed wildly with it, sending every maid and eunuch scrambling for cover.

The Worthy Dowager Consort came in with her attendants and called out sharply, "Have you had enough?"

An'yang threw down the whip. Her voice was raw with resentment. "Mother Consort — I refuse to accept it. I refuse! Why should that worthless woman get to be Empress while I am being married off to filth!"

The Worthy Dowager Consort felt her blood run cold. She stepped forward and struck An'yang across the face. "Stop talking! Swallow every one of those words."

An'yang pressed her hand to her cheek, eyes wide. "Mother Consort — you hit me?"

The Worthy Dowager Consort's palm was still trembling slightly. Her face was iron-grey, and she looked at An'yang with both disappointment and grief. "An'yang! Think about where you stand now before you open your mouth! Do you still not understand why you ended up in this marriage? This Consort cannot protect you forever, and the Xie family cannot help you either. Every word you say like that, if it gets out, will only make your situation worse. Be quiet and stop causing trouble!"

An'yang's face burned. She could not hear any of it. She pressed her hand to her cheek, crying, and went back to her room and shut the door.

The Worthy Dowager Consort stood where she was. She was beginning to regret how she had indulged An'yang and failed to discipline her.

Things were not what they had been. The Emperor had proclaimed his Empress before the entire court — Jiang Mi was no longer someone An'yang could afford to speak of with contempt. A princess the Emperor did not protect, who had already made an enemy of the Empress — with An'yang's nature, her life in a husband's household was going to be a misery.

......

The news of the new Emperor naming a daughter of the former Cheng'en Marquess family as Empress spread through the entire capital with wings.

In the Shen family study, Shen Chānghéng held his brush and tried to write — and could not calm himself.

His wife, Madam Hé, pushed open the door and came in, her face troubled. "Husband — how can you just sit there? How could the Emperor have named a Jiang girl as Empress?"

Shen Chānghéng did not look up. He continued to write. "Why should I not be sitting? The Emperor has his reasons for choosing his Empress. What right do you have to say more?"

Madam Hé said urgently, "But — but was not the Empress's position being kept for Āwēi?"

Shen Chānghéng slapped the brush down. "What nonsense are you talking!"

Madam Hé was startled by the sudden outburst from her usually mild-tempered husband, and felt very aggrieved at the same time. "Husband — after Yǎoróng passed away, the Emperor showed the Shen family such great favour and still did not name an Empress. Was he not waiting for Yǎowēi to come of age?"

Shen Chānghéng fell silent. He had once harboured that thought himself.

Of the families who had rendered service in the Emperor's rise to the throne, which of them had not nurtured some hope of their daughter becoming Empress? The Shen family's legitimate daughter had been the Emperor's former betrothed — they had a stronger claim than other families. After the Emperor ascended, he had continued to hold off on naming an Empress or consorts. After the Shen family threw in their lot with the Emperor and the Emperor had pledged not to fail them, it was difficult not to think that perhaps — with Yǎowēi not yet of age — the Emperor was waiting for her.

But today's investiture edict had struck him like a blow to the head. He now saw clearly: the Emperor had cleared the path for his own entry into the Grand Secretariat; Qiānxiū had topped the examinations and entered the Hànlín Academy — all of this had already been a clear road upward for the Shen family.

And yet they had gone on coveting that empress's position on top of it all. They had been inexcusably greedy.

Shen Chānghéng felt ashamed and guilty and a thread of dread — could this also be the Emperor's way of delivering a warning?

He said in a measured voice, "Madam — begin calling on other families and look into prospects for Yǎowēi."

Madam Hé was startled and confused. She had just opened her mouth to speak when there was a crash — Shen Yǎowēi, who had been crouching outside the door listening, tumbled in.

She fell to the floor and wept. "Father — I do not want to be looked at for a match. The Empress's position should have been mine. Mother said so. Grandmother said so. Every cousin and sister envied me. Everywhere I went, the ladies and their daughters all understood without needing to say it — I was the one who would enter the palace and stand at the Emperor's side. It must have been the Jiang family who used some scheme to make the Emperor give them the investiture. Father — you cannot simply stand by and do nothing."

Shen Yǎowēi had completely shed the composed, self-possessed manner she usually kept. She had nowhere left to place her hopes but her father.

Shen Chānghéng flew into a fury. He pointed at Shen Yǎowēi and turned to his wife. "Is this the daughter you raised? Something I myself never dared to be certain of — and you treated it as though everyone simply understood it? You told her the Emperor would give her the Empress's position out of respect for her sister's memory? How could you be so foolish! You are going to bring ruin on the Shen family!"

He shouted toward the door: "Someone come — take the young miss back to her room and keep her there. She is not to step outside."

At his order, women servants came in immediately. Shen Yǎowēi had never been treated like this. She struggled and called to Madam Hé for help. "Mother — Mother, please speak for me! I do not want to be locked up. Father — I am going to be a consort in the palace. You cannot lock me away!"

Shen Chānghéng's expression changed completely. "Gag her and get her out of here!"

Three strong servants complied and hauled Shen Yǎowēi away.

Madam Hé was in a panic. She wanted to go after her but dared not provoke Shen Chānghéng further. "Husband — Yǎowēi is saying things she does not mean because she is upset. I will talk sense into her."

Shen Chānghéng was quiet for a moment. He looked toward the outer courtyard. "Find her a husband quickly — and have her married out of the capital."

Madam Hé's eyes filled with tears. "Husband — I will find someone for Yǎowēi. But please let her stay in the capital."

Shen Chānghéng sighed. "Look at her — raving like someone who has lost her wits. Can she stay in the capital?"

What Shen Yǎowēi had just screamed aloud — if those words spread, suspicions would be aroused.

After Madam Hé left, Shen Chānghéng summoned Shen Qiānxiū.

He looked at his son's lost, hollow expression and thought only: what a catastrophe.

"What are you thinking now?" he asked.

In recent days Shen Qiānxiū had been finding every way he could to avoid the Duke Ningguo's family match, and had finally come clean with his parents about his true feelings and begged them to go and sound out the Jiang family's wishes. He had been almost on the point of persuading them — and then the Emperor named his Empress.

The girl he admired was entering the imperial palace to become the mother of a nation. Even the hope of seeing her again would be an extravagance.

Shen Qiānxiū heard his father's question and was long silent.

Shen Chānghéng said, "Since you do not care for the Duke Ningguo's daughter, I will not force you. But you must be engaged. Your cousin on the Hé side has waited two years for you. You should..."

"Father," Shen Qiānxiū interrupted. "I do not want to be engaged yet."

Shen Chānghéng knew his son's stubborn nature. He said with deep feeling, "Qiānxiū — do not make yourself a thorn in the Emperor's side."

With that, he shook his head and left the study.

......

The Minister of the Board of Rites came to the Jiang residence bearing the investiture edict. The Imperial Household Department sent the imperial betrothal gifts — the procession stretched beyond sight.

The entire Jiang household knelt to receive the edict.

The Minister read aloud: "We observe that virtue aligned with the Yellow Robe must have its foundation in the inner palace. The daughter of the Cheng'en Duke, Miss Jiang, comes of distinguished lineage, favoured by auspicious stars, gentle in disposition and virtuous in character, refined in manner and dignified in bearing. Let the grand ceremony of investiture be established, and with the golden register and golden seal, We hereby name her as Empress..."

Jiang Mi received the edict with both hands and rose.

The Minister then read a second edict, raising Jiang Qingxuān, Assistant Minister of the Board of Works, to the title of Cheng'en Duke.

When both edicts had been read, the Minister bowed to Jiang Mi. His assistant presented the golden register and golden seal.

Jiang Mi took them in hand. The assembled company offered the salute due to a ruler. "May Her Highness the Empress be blessed with eternal peace."

The Imperial Household Department then carried in the imperial betrothal gifts one by one.

Everyone in the Jiang family had a feeling of unreality.

In the very moment of the family's decline, Jiang Mi had been named Empress. Her father had been given the title of Duke.

The Jiang family had risen another step. When the Empress Dowager had been named Empress in her time, the late Emperor had only given the Jiang family a Marquessate. This time it was a Dukedom.

The date of the imperial wedding was set for the ninth day of the seventh month — less than a month away. Everything was rushed.

Everyone felt the time was too short, that much could not be prepared in such haste. But the Board of Astronomy had named that day as the auspicious date, the Emperor had approved it, and no one dared raise an objection.

Fortunately the Imperial Household Department had prepared nearly everything already.

The Jiang family also gathered all its resources to add to Jiang Mi's trousseau.

The Empress Dowager sent a female court official to assist with preparations and to guide her in proper ceremony.

In late sixth month, the day of Jiang Yì's wedding arrived.

Many who had not received invitations came to offer congratulations regardless. Officials' wives who had not been in regular contact sent gifts. Everyone in the Jiang household understood clearly why.

This time Jiang Mi was able to watch Jiang Yì leave in person.

Before getting into the bridal sedan, Jiang Yì wept bitterly. Jiang Mi cried along with her. However fine a marriage — going to live in someone else's household was never as easy as being a daughter at home.

Jiang Mi could not help feeling a touch of wistfulness. But the Zhang young master treated Sister Yi very well.

After that celebration, it would very soon be Jiang Mi's turn.

The wedding ceremonial robes had been made in the palace. Jiang Mi had had time only to embroider her own wedding veil.

Since the investiture edict was proclaimed, she and Xiao Huaiyan had not seen each other.

As the date drew closer, Jiang Mi grew more anxious by the day. She took out the edict Xiao Huaiyan had given her and read it over several times before she could settle a little.

On the eve of the wedding, Qiuyu came in to say, "Miss — Madam is here."

Jiang Mi put down what she was holding. "Ask her in quickly."

Su-shi walked into the room and curtseyed. "Your Highness — may you be blessed with peace."

Jiang Mi smiled. "Madam, there is no need for that. Please sit."

Su-shi sat down, not quite sure how to begin. She chatted with Jiang Mi for a while about the trousseau, asked about the wedding proceedings, and had drunk a full cup of tea.

Jiang Mi could see she had something on her mind. "Madam — please just say what you came to say."

Su-shi drew a small booklet from her sleeve and handed it over. "Your Highness — have a look at this first. If there is anything you do not understand — I will... I will explain it."

Jiang Mi opened the booklet and quietly went red.

The illustrations were considerably more detailed and explicit than the material the Empress Dowager's matron had shown her. Jiang Mi shut it immediately.

Su-shi took a sip of water to mask her own awkwardness. "This came by sea trade — the painting style is a little different from ours. Your Highness just needs to understand the general idea."

Su-shi herself had been given a booklet by her mother before her own wedding, and she had thought to do the same for Jiang Mi.

Jiang Mi knew it was meant kindly. She nodded, her face red.

But looking at the booklet, she could not help thinking of the first time she had been summoned to the bedchamber in the last life — how she had danced an exotic dance to try to attract Xiao Huaiyan's favour. Xiao Huaiyan had been fierce and urgent and she had suffered for it.

What Xiao Huaiyan did in practice was far more outrageous than anything in that booklet...

Jiang Mi gave a long sigh and sat on the edge of the bed, dreading tomorrow more than ever.

chapters.title: Chapter 104
chapters.content:
Jiang Mi had not slept well. She turned and turned and could not rest, and by the time the sky was just beginning to lighten, she had already opened her eyes.

She pushed back the quilt, put on her embroidered slippers, draped a robe over her shoulders, and sat at her dressing table looking at herself in the mirror.

Her complexion was still reasonable. Only those almond eyes held a faint anxiety and wistfulness.

In the last life she had also entered the palace in the seventh month — then, her aunt had passed away, and Xiao Huaiyan had honoured a deathbed wish by bringing her in.

This seventh month she was entering the palace too. As Xiao Huaiyan's wife.

Jiang Mi could not quite name what she felt. Apprehension still lurked in her chest — yet somewhere beneath it was the same faint thread of longing she had always had, even in the last life.

Was this time truly different?

Jiang Mi finished the morning meal, and the women of the Jiang household came one by one.

Her mother's side of the family had only her maternal uncle's branch left. When she was named Empress, her uncle's whole family had made the journey from Qingzhou. Her uncle and her two male cousins had gone with her father to receive guests in the front courtyard. Her aunt by marriage, Madam Yú, arrived with her cousin-daughter Qín Sīwǎn.

Her mother and her uncle had been born of the same parents. After her mother passed away, her uncle's family had remained in Qingzhou, sending gifts at every festival. The visits had been infrequent, but there was warmth in seeing them.

Palace women and court officials helped Jiang Mi into the bridal ceremonial robes and set the phoenix crown on her head.

The female court official dressing her could not help but marvel inwardly: this Empress Jiang had a beauty seldom seen in the world. Her face was already radiant without much adornment — a touch of rouge to her lips and she was more vivid still. In the bridal court robes, the delicate beauty held its own regal grace.

The Jiang sisters all gathered around Jiang Mi, talking softly. That Qín girl had a very sweet tongue — one moment 'Elder Cousin is so lovely', the next 'Elder Cousin is dignified and virtuous'.

Jiang Mi noticed that Jiang Róng's mood was subdued and she had not said much. She beckoned her over and took her hand. "What is wrong, A-Róng?"

Jiang Róng heard her elder sister's gentle voice and sniffled. "I don't want Elder Sister to go..." Her mother had told her that once Elder Sister entered the palace, seeing her would be much harder. Not like Second Elder Sister, who could visit and be visited.

Jiang Yì, so recently married herself, heard this and laughed. "A-Róng — you really are still a child. In another couple of years, you will be getting married yourself."

Jiang Mi knew Jiang Róng depended on her. She said, "If you miss me, come to the palace. I will have someone sent to bring you."

Jiang Róng's eyes lit up at once. She nodded shyly with a smile.

Qín Sīwǎn, standing nearby, followed suit. "Elder Cousin — you cannot play favourites. Sīwǎn will miss you too."

Her words earned small frowns from both Jiang Wǎn and Jiang Yì, though neither said anything.

Jiang Mi only smiled and did not reply.

Jiang Róng was not sure whether she had said the wrong thing and caused her elder sister trouble.

Just then Qiuyu came in and announced, "Your Highness — the bridal phoenix palanquin is nearly here. You are needed at the main gate."

Everyone in the room stirred and rose.

The court official helped Jiang Mi to her feet. The whole party followed her out.

The wedding procession arrived at dusk.

The Emperor's envoy led a vast retinue. The imperial guards cleared the road ahead. The citizens of the capital lined both sides of the street to watch.

A wedding of the Emperor and Empress was a spectacle rarely seen in a generation.

The phoenix palanquin stopped before the gates of the Cheng'en Duke's house.

Jiang Qingxuān, Jiang Qingdé, Jiang Hóng, and the rest all stood waiting in the front courtyard.

They saw Jiang Mi come through the gates surrounded by her ladies and court officials, and all of them bowed.

Jiang Qingxuān looked at Jiang Mi, escorted through the procession of women, and was moved beyond words. The Empress's honour carried the Jiang family's glory forward — and yet life in the palace was never easy.

He came to stand before her. His eyes had reddened. His voice came out tight. "Your Highness — take good care of yourself."

Jiang Mi held back her tears and nodded.

Outside, the ceremony official was calling out: requesting the Empress's Highness to board the phoenix palanquin.

Jiang Qingxuān took the phoenix-embroidered wedding veil from the waiting maidservant and laid it over Jiang Mi.

Then he pulled back his court robes and knelt. "We send the Empress off with all our wishes for joy and happiness."

The entire Jiang family knelt, and their voices came in unison: "We send the Empress off with all our wishes for joy and happiness."

Beneath the veil, Jiang Mi wept without sound as the court official helped her step by step toward the phoenix palanquin.

All along the route of the Empress's phoenix palanquin, the people called out and pressed forward to see.

The upper floors of every teahouse were packed, watching the imperial wedding procession's splendour — exclaiming, wondering, talking.

Shen Qiānxiū stood at a window and watched the yellow-gold procession pass below. The phoenix palanquin hid the person inside from view — but this was already the closest he would ever be to her. From here on, she was his sovereign and he her subject.

The procession passed through the Duān Gate, the Wǔ Gate, and the Tàihé Gate into the palace.

Jiang Mi was carried all the way into the Kūnníng Palace.

She stepped down from the phoenix palanquin and was helped by court officials to sit on the dragon-and-phoenix wedding bed. The maids who had accompanied her from home came in with the palace attendants.

The court official who had been managing the Kūnníng Palace came forward with a tray of food and said to Jiang Mi, "Your Highness — His Majesty is still at the banquet with his ministers. He will not come for some time. Please eat something to sustain yourself."

Jiang Mi was indeed hungry — and tired. And knowing Xiao Huaiyan would be here soon made her more anxious by the moment.

She lifted her veil. The court official standing nearby appeared to be in her early thirties, with a fine-featured look.

Jiang Mi was not sure whether she was someone arranged by the Empress Dowager or by Xiao Huaiyan. She nodded. "Thank you, Matron."

The official bowed hurriedly. "Your Highness is too kind."

Jiang Mi drank a small bowl of soup, ate a few pieces of steamed sweet curd, and stopped.

The court official had the palace maids help Jiang Mi wash and freshen up, then helped her replace the wedding veil.

Before long, the sound of greeting came from outside.

Jiang Mi quietly curled her hands into fists inside her sleeves and held her back very straight.

Xiao Huaiyan came around the screen. He looked at the figure sitting upright before the wedding bed. His eyes, somewhat heavy with wine, watched quietly.

A smile spread at his lips.

At last. She had come back to him.

He walked toward her and took the scale balance the court official offered him, and lifted the veil.

Jiang Mi looked up. Xiao Huaiyan was in his imperial wedding robes, a red-pearl gold crown on his head, his face brilliantly handsome in the light of the dragon-and-phoenix candles.

His phoenix eyes, slightly unfocused with wine, were enough to make her face flush and her pulse quicken just looking at him.

Jiang Mi felt both flustered and self-conscious under that gaze — but there was nowhere to hide. Xiao Huaiyan came and sat down beside her.

She could smell the wine on him — heavier than usual.

The court official presented the wedding wine.

Both Xiao Huaiyan and Jiang Mi took their cups. Sitting very close together, Xiao Huaiyan held out his cup toward Jiang Mi. She lifted her arm and looped it around his, holding up her own cup.

Xiao Huaiyan smiled, and drank it all at once.

Jiang Mi gripped her cup firmly — she remembered that the wedding wine was to be drunk to the last drop. Though the wine was sharp and burning, she drank it down with him.

The moment she finished, her face felt even hotter.

The ceremony complete, the court officials and palace maids all withdrew.

"Tangtan." His voice was low and rough.

Jiang Mi felt the breathing beside her go heavier. Her chin was tilted up. Something warm pressed to her lips, coaxing them open bit by bit. She was forced to tip her head back, lips parting slightly.

She was lightly, deliberately bitten — not hard, not soft — ground against with a numbing sweetness until she felt dizzy. It was not only the wedding wine she had drunk — Xiao Huaiyan's own wine-soaked breath was enough to intoxicate her.

Jiang Mi's breathing grew more disordered. The entanglement went deeper, and the tip of her tongue went numb.

She drew in a breath and tried to pull back.

Xiao Huaiyan followed the retreat and pressed forward. One hand closed around her slender waist; the other moved to undo her ceremonial robes.

The phoenix crown was heavy on her head. And the weight of Xiao Huaiyan coming over her was heavier still — she could barely breathe.

Jiang Mi, unable to bear the relentless press of it, opened her mouth and bit down.

Xiao Huaiyan went still. The sharp pain cleared his head a little. He pulled back and looked at her, a teasing sweep of his gaze before he reluctantly lifted himself.

The tips of his phoenix eyes were faintly red. He rubbed the furrow between his brows, steadied her, and reached up to lift the phoenix crown from her head. "I was too hasty."

He pressed his thumb to Jiang Mi's lips and rubbed gently. "Tangtan — I am very happy today. I drank a little more than usual. Do not be afraid. I will not hurt you."

Without the crown, she could breathe again. But his words gave her no comfort — she knew there was no way out of tonight.

The wedding wine was catching up with her now, a faint swimming in her head. She said hesitantly, "Your Majesty — should you not first sober up a little?"

His mind was clear. He heard her voice, soft and yielding. His gaze went dark. He held her around the waist and lowered her back into the bed hangings. "The best remedy for wine is right before me. Why reach further when what I need is here?"

Xiao Huaiyan pulled at his own collar, loosened his waist sash, and shrugged off the ceremonial robes, dropping them to the floor.

An embroidered slipper rolled off the edge of the bed.

The silk stockings disappeared. Bare, pale feet curled tight against the red wedding bedding in apprehension.

The burning grip of his hands enclosed her ankles and moved slowly upward. Xiao Huaiyan shifted his position.

Jiang Mi's face blazed. She kicked and struggled and it made no difference at all.

She turned her face to bury it in the quilt, biting down on her own hand.

But Xiao Huaiyan seemed almost to be doing it deliberately. Jiang Mi tried hard to press back the soft sounds that kept threatening to escape — and could not entirely.

The magnificent empress robes were scattered across the bed. On the red brocade, a pale trembling.

Xiao Huaiyan raised his head and pulled her arms up, guiding them to wrap around his neck.

Jiang Mi's hair was in disarray. Both arms had gone weak. Those almond eyes, misted before, suddenly opened wide, and her fingers gripped his shoulders hard.

Xiao Huaiyan's eyes were very dark. He bent his head and kissed her gently, as though soothing.

The tears in Jiang Mi's eyes slid free. Xiao Huaiyan drew one across his lips and pressed them to her mouth. "I will be slower. Do not be afraid."

The tears were not from pain. It was the sensation of losing all control — like a small boat adrift on a vast ocean, being broken apart and swallowed by wind and waves.

Jiang Mi trembled without being able to help it. Her waist was held in a grip she could not move against. She let out small, thin sounds — which gradually softened and grew sweet...

Xiao Huaiyan drew her up against him, settling her against his chest. Smooth hair like silk fell in cascades across her back, just enough to hint at faint red traces left on pale skin.

Jiang Mi breathed in and out, still not recovered. Xiao Huaiyan stroked her hair — wherever his hand passed, she still could not help a slow dissolving.

Xiao Huaiyan wound a strand of her hair around his finger. "Tangtan — there is one ceremony we have not yet completed."

She had no desire to answer him. Whatever the ceremony — she had no strength left.

She said nothing and pretended to be asleep. Knowing Xiao Huaiyan as she did, she was afraid he was not nearly finished and did not want to provoke anything further.

Xiao Huaiyan gave her earlobe a small bite to make her turn.

Jiang Mi could not hold out. She opened her eyes.

She saw Xiao Huaiyan had taken a small knife from somewhere. In one quick motion, a lock of her hair fell into his hand. He cut a lock of his own as well.

He wove the two locks together, and those unfathomable phoenix eyes looked at her. "We two are bound by this lock of hair, tied in one heart. The ceremony is now complete."

chapters.title: Chapter 105
chapters.content:
Jiang Mi stared at the braided knot of hair in Xiao Huaiyan's hand. Her eyes ached and stung. An emotion she could not name surged up from somewhere inside her.

Tears welled and spilled, running down into the curve of his neck.

Jiang Mi pressed herself against Xiao Huaiyan's chest and shook with quiet, helpless trembling.

Xiao Huaiyan stroked her back again and again, gathering her in close. He said softly, "The fault was mine. I let you suffer so much."

Jiang Mi bit her lip. She had not meant to cry. But his words made the tears impossible to stop.

She had never dared to truly believe any of this. These days had felt like a dream she was afraid to wake from.

When she saw him weave their two locks of hair together, something settled in her chest — she no longer felt quite so unmoored, no longer grasped at everything while fearing to lose it.

Xiao Huaiyan tilted her chin up. Their eyes met. Jiang Mi's face was flushed, her eyes shining and liquid. He said, "Tangtan — from here on, let us live well together."

Jiang Mi pressed her lips together. Her throat was so tight she could not speak.

Slowly, she reached out and quietly wrapped her arms around his waist.

Something flickered in Xiao Huaiyan's eyes. This was the first time she had reached for him herself.

His gaze burned. He bent down, lips catching her tears and brushing slowly over her mouth, deepening the kiss.

Jiang Mi's body went soft and yielding. She let herself be drawn along, and the sounds she made only made her face flush deeper.

Her waist was pressed and kneaded, not painfully but persistently. Her earlobe was gently caught between his teeth. "Are you recovered?"

Jiang Mi was pulled from her breath by his touch. She knew he was not finished. She buried her face in his shoulder and said in a muffled voice, "No — not..."

Xiao Huaiyan paused. His voice went low and rough. "Does it hurt?"

What was she supposed to say to that? At first it had hurt — but he was more patient and restrained than in the last life, and gradually what she felt could not exactly be called pain, more a kind of slipping loss of control that frightened her. She was embarrassed and at a loss and could not help scratching lightly at his arm.

Xiao Huaiyan gave a low laugh.

He held her still. "Tangtan — stop catching your breath. Stop trembling."

Jiang Mi clung to his shoulder and cried softly. She was so tired she could barely keep her eyes open.

Xiao Huaiyan put on an outer robe and wrapped her in a cloak and lifted her, carrying her outside.

The maids and eunuchs attending outside the Kūnníng Palace sleeping chamber were standing much further away than usual.

The personal maids who had accompanied Jiang Mi into the palace, listening to the sounds that had come from within, were every one of them red-faced.

Qiuyu was the most composed of the group. She stole a glance at the other palace maids and eunuchs all standing with bowed heads and carefully blank expressions, then signalled to Chūnhuí and Xiàruò to collect themselves and not embarrass their mistress.

Li Fu had been keeping close watch on the room. When he heard the door, he saw the Emperor carrying the Empress — wrapped in a cloak — out of the chamber and heading directly for the bathhouse.

Li Fu gave his whisk a flick and followed with his attendants.

He paused and looked back at Qiuyu and the others, offering a few words of guidance: "Get in there and tidy the room. Then take clean clothes for Her Highness to the bathhouse."

He finished and hurried away.

Qiuyu and the rest went in immediately. They found clothing scattered across the floor — the small embroidered inner robe with its peony vine pattern was particularly conspicuous. With red faces they opened the windows to air the room and changed out all the bedding. Qiuyu found what she was looking for in the tangle of crumpled quilts and put it away with care.

Jiang Mi, barely awake, was lowered into warm water. Then the burning heat came up behind her.

Jiang Mi was pressed against the side of the pool. She gasped in rapid breaths. "Don't — stop — Your Majesty, I cannot anymore, I truly cannot."

Xiao Huaiyan glanced downward, at what swayed with the water.

His iron grip held her waist. "Yes. I know."

He knew. But he did not seem to be stopping. Jiang Mi could barely stay upright. She put her arms around his neck to brace herself or she would have slipped beneath the water.

Jiang Mi was lifted out of the pool and carried, draped over his shoulder, making small, limp sounds like a spent kitten.

Xiao Huaiyan brought her out of the water, dried her completely, tossed the cloth aside, and helped her into clean, cool inner garments.

She was set down on the bed in the sleeping chamber. She turned onto her side with her back to Xiao Huaiyan.

Although Xiao Huaiyan had held himself back in the bathhouse, he had still made her cry more than once while helping her bathe.

Xiao Huaiyan held a small jade vial. He sat beside her on the bed and nudged her waist. "Are you genuinely asleep?"

Jiang Mi lay still and silent.

He reached for the tie on her inner robe. "Then I will apply the salve."

Jiang Mi went rigid. Apply what salve?

She felt where his hand was headed and quickly pressed it down. "No — no need."

Nothing was truly injured.

Xiao Huaiyan lay down along her back, a light nip at her earlobe. "I am not easy about it. And I am not looking — you can just lie still."

Jiang Mi's face burned. She felt the medicine — cool, clean, light.

Xiao Huaiyan withdrew his hand, wiped it on a cloth, and pulled her toward him. "All right. Sleep."

Xiao Huaiyan ran naturally warm. He was pressed against her back, and she shifted a little further from him. "Hot."

Xiao Huaiyan glanced at the blocks of ice kept in the room. He rolled her into his arms, unhurried. "I am warm too. But you feel good."

Jiang Mi was too sleepy to keep her eyes open. She stopped arguing with Xiao Huaiyan and let herself be held.

Late in the night, she turned in her sleep and curled naturally against him.

......

The next morning, Jiang Mi woke to a deep ache in her back. The man who had been lying beside her was already dressed in imperial robes, seated at the table with a cup of tea, reading something — a memorial, it looked like.

Xiao Huaiyan heard her stir and set the memorial down. He came and rested a hand gently on her face. "You looked so exhausted — I let you sleep a little longer."

Jiang Mi thought: who made me so exhausted?

She remembered the ceremonies of the day — she asked, "What time is it? We have not missed the time?"

"The time is just right," he said. "Get up and eat something, then come with me."

He had barely finished speaking before a court official came in leading Qiuyu and several maids, together with various palace women, to attend to Jiang Mi.

Jiang Mi changed into the formal phoenix robes with the court official's help. The phoenix crown too was changed — this one was different in style from the wedding crown, though equally magnificent.

Under Xiao Huaiyan's gaze, Jiang Mi felt a little self-conscious.

In the last life, after she had been summoned to the bedchamber, Xiao Huaiyan would generally have gone to morning court by the time she woke. She would find herself alone. It was rare to have Xiao Huaiyan waiting while she dressed and had her hair done.

And he had stopped reading the memorial entirely. That gaze had come over here — which only made her more nervous.

The morning meal was brought in. Jiang Mi looked at the table full of food, glanced at Xiao Huaiyan, and asked, "Has Your Majesty eaten?"

Xiao Huaiyan rose and came toward her. "Not yet. I was waiting for you."

Jiang Mi stood to serve him. Xiao Huaiyan took her hand and drew her down to sit with him. "I told you a long time ago not to serve me. From now on we eat together."

He ladled a bowl of Seven-Herb Broth and pushed it toward her.

Jiang Mi looked at the bowl of Seven-Herb Broth. In the last life she had made this broth for him — she liked it and had wanted to share it with him. He had tasted it at the time, said nothing particular, and she had never been sure whether he enjoyed it or not. She had not dared make it for him again.

She wondered now whether the imperial kitchen had hit on her preference by coincidence.

She drank her soup quietly. Xiao Huaiyan occasionally placed something on her plate. Jiang Mi ate a piece of silver fish — then reached out with her own chopsticks and added a dish of plain braised tripe to his plate.

Xiao Huaiyan raised an eyebrow. He said nothing, and ate what she had given him.

When they finished the morning meal, they walked out of the sleeping chamber.

The maids and eunuchs standing outside all bowed: "May the Emperor and the Empress be blessed with eternal peace."

The imperial palanquin and the phoenix palanquin both stood waiting outside the Kūnníng Palace.

Jiang Mi was making her way toward the phoenix palanquin when Xiao Huaiyan, already seated in the imperial palanquin, called over to her. "Tangtan — come here."

Jiang Mi's expression showed surprise. Seeing that he was not joking, she walked toward him.

The palanquin had not been raised. No one could move.

She hesitated. Was it really appropriate for her and Xiao Huaiyan to share the imperial palanquin to the Fengxiān Hall together?

But under his gaze, she went to him.

She took Li Fu's hand to help her up and settled beside Xiao Huaiyan.

The moment she was seated, the palanquin rose.

She looked back. The empty phoenix palanquin followed behind, with attending court officials and palace maids. Qiuyu and the others were not in the procession.

Xiao Huaiyan covered her hand, resting on her knee, with his own. "It is only a formal ceremony. There is no need to be nervous."

Jiang Mi nodded.

He smiled. "The court official managing your affairs is named Sun — she was chosen by me. Try her out for now and see if she suits you. If you find her not quite to your liking, ask the Empress Dowager's side to arrange someone else. Your own maids still need time to learn the palace rules — let them settle in first."

Jiang Mi looked at him. She had not expected Xiao Huaiyan to be saying these things to her. Official Sun must be the court official who had led proceedings — dressing her, managing the meals.

She said quietly, "Thank you, Your Majesty. Official Sun is very capable."

Xiao Huaiyan squeezed her soft hands. "Then how do you plan to thank me? An ordinary token of thanks is not something I accept."

Jiang Mi could tell from his eyes that he was being playful. She knew exactly what he meant.

She looked away with pink cheeks. How was he always so hungry for that?

The journey was not long. The two of them exchanged few words, but a question always had an answer. It was remarkably easy.

Before long they reached the Fengxiān Hall.

The Fengxiān Hall enshrined portraits of emperors and empresses of every generation.

When a new emperor took an empress, he would bring her here to pay their respects to the imperial ancestors.

Jiang Mi received incense from the ritual official and paid her respects alongside Xiao Huaiyan.

Then they left the Fengxiān Hall and made their way to the Tàihé Hall.

The square before the Tàihé Hall was filled with civil and military officials who had been waiting a long time. Under the full blaze of the sun, many of them were sweating through their robes.

When the auspicious hour arrived and the Emperor appeared on the Tàihé Hall steps, the assembled officials all prostrated themselves in salute.

The newly named Empress Jiang, led by the ritual official, walked up the Nine Dragon steps of the vermillion dais — one step at a time, walking toward the Son of Heaven.

Jiang Mi looked up at Xiao Huaiyan, high above.

She was walking toward him.

The young emperor watched the Empress coming nearer and nearer. He smiled and extended his hand toward her.

When Jiang Mi placed her hand in his and stood at Xiao Huaiyan's side, the ritual official read the investiture edict aloud, proclaiming to all under heaven that Jiang Shi had become the Empress of Great Wei.

Jiang Mi looked out from where she stood. Below, the kneeling officials' voices filled the air in an unceasing wave of congratulation.

chapters.title: Grand Finale
chapters.content:
Coming out of the Tàihé Hall, Jiang Mi and Xiao Huaiyan made their way together to the Ci'ning Palace.

Xiao Huaiyan held her hand and kept her beside him on the imperial palanquin.

All along the way, word spread quietly through the palace of the Emperor's great favour toward the Empress.

Inside the Ci'ning Palace, the Empress Dowager was waiting with eager eyes. She had stationed Qīngxuě at the hall doorway and sent little palace maids to stand watch along the palace lane.

Matron Cuī laughed and coaxed her: "Your Highness, do not be anxious. The Emperor and the Empress are still at the Tàihé Hall receiving the congratulations of the assembled officials. They will be here before long."

The Empress Dowager understood. She had once done this herself — stood beside the late Emperor in the Tàihé Hall and received the court's obeisance. Her own family had been unremarkable; she had been chosen as Empress by the Empress Dowager of that era because her fortune had been read as the phoenix destiny. The Jiang family and she herself had been overjoyed — a single morning had changed the family's fate entirely. She had entered the palace full of longing and hope, only to be met with the late Emperor's coldness. She had watched the barely suppressed impatience on his face, watched his back as he left, and felt hope after hope give out beneath her. She could not allow herself even a sliver of grievance; she had to manage the six palaces with magnanimous grace, to yield and step back before the women he favoured. Entering the palace had only been the beginning. She could only hope that her Tangtan would be luckier than she had been.

About half an hour later, a little palace maid came running in to report: "Your Highness the Empress Dowager — the imperial palanquin is on its way."

The Empress Dowager smoothed her sleeves and sat up straight. She noticed something odd in the little maid's expression. "Is there something else?"

The palace maid's face was bright with barely contained happiness. "Your Highness — Her Highness the Empress has come together with the Emperor, sharing the imperial palanquin."

The Empress Dowager's prayer beads went still in her hand.

Matron Cuī was all smiles. "Your Highness — is this not the best of news? The Emperor's favour toward the Empress is evident for all to see!" She knew well what the Empress Dowager had feared. When the Empress Dowager herself had been newly named Empress, the late Emperor had cited pressing matters and left her to go to the Ci'ning Palace alone. That gesture had cost the Empress Dowager her dignity — the entire palace had known, from that moment, that the Empress was not in the Emperor's favour.

Now the Emperor had come with the Empress, sharing the same palanquin. This was an uncommon show of imperial grace.

The Empress Dowager felt the weight she had been carrying ease a little. She had been afraid of arousing the Emperor's suspicion, and had not dared to place even a single attendant in the Kūnníng Palace, even knowing that Tangtan would soon be its mistress.

Outside, a eunuch called out in a loud, carrying voice: "The Emperor and Her Highness the Empress have arrived."

When Jiang Mi stepped down from the imperial palanquin, Xiao Huaiyan caught her at the waist.

The spot was already aching, and the touch made it give way beneath her — she nearly stumbled.

Jiang Mi's face went red. She glanced quickly around her; fortunately the palace maids and eunuchs all had their heads bowed and no one had seen.

Xiao Huaiyan leaned close to her ear. "When we return, shall I rub it for you?"

She looked up and saw him smiling. She could not help glaring at him.

His smile only deepened.

The Emperor and Empress entered the Ci'ning Palace hand in hand.

The Empress Dowager watched Jiang Mi walk in — flushed, faintly shy, something eased in her expression — and could not help but smile. It seemed she had not been made to suffer on her wedding night.

Jiang Mi and Xiao Huaiyan came forward together and made their obeisance.

Jiang Mi took the teacup from a palace maid's hands and offered it to the Empress Dowager. "This concubine respectfully greets the Empress Mother and presents her with tea." This time she no longer called her Aunt.

The Empress Dowager said all the right things and had Jiang Mi rise. She accepted the cup and drank from it, then lifted a rosewood box from Matron Cuī's tray.

She opened it. Inside was a bracelet — a Hundred Birds Honouring the Phoenix design, the workmanship so fine it seemed impossible by mortal hands.

"This was given to me by the Grand Empress Dowager when I entered the palace. Now I pass this Hundred Birds bracelet to you. May you and the Emperor be united in heart forever and be blessed with many children."

Jiang Mi received it with both hands. "Thank you, Empress Mother."

The Empress Dowager smiled with deep contentment. She glanced at the Emperor, and saw that his gaze was resting on Tangtan.

A flash of surprise crossed the Empress Dowager's eyes, followed by another quiet smile.

Looking at this — the Emperor's choice of a Jiang woman as Empress was not purely a matter of checking the influence of outside families.

Tangtan was truly luckier than she had been.

......

After leaving the Ci'ning Palace, Jiang Mi returned to the Kūnníng Palace to receive the obeisances of the noble ladies — women of the imperial family and the official wives of the fourth rank and above.

Xiao Huaiyan went to the Jiāotài Hall to receive his ministers.

Jiang Mi rode the phoenix palanquin back to the Kūnníng Palace alone this time.

The imperial clan women and official wives waiting to be admitted were all gathered outside the Kūnníng Palace, watching the yellow imperial procession carry the phoenix palanquin slowly toward them.

Everyone bowed. "Long live Her Highness the Empress."

After the palanquin passed inside, the presiding palace maid summoned them in to pay their respects.

The noble ladies saw this young Empress and did not dare show the slightest discourtesy. Many of them harboured other thoughts inwardly — but could only offer their respectful congratulations.

Jiang Mi sat in the seat of honour and looked at the familiar and unfamiliar faces bowing to her. Her heart was full of feeling.

Since her rebirth, she had never once imagined she would reach this point.

Among those faces, she saw An'yang — going through the motions with barely concealed resentment. She saw Su-shi, a little nervous but flushed with happiness. She saw Grand Secretary Shen's wife, and the mother-in-law of Sister Yi...

Jiang Mi did not keep them long. When the ceremony was done she sent them all on their way.

The noble ladies filed out of the Kūnníng Palace, more than a few of them curious about this Empress. They had never before encountered a situation where the Emperor named an Empress without naming a single consort alongside. Now that they had seen this Empress in person, they understood a little — who could bear to see such a beauty made to suffer? Even so — how could an emperor's inner palace have only one woman? More would surely be added in time.

They had only to wait.

But those women waited until the Emperor named a Crown Prince, waited until the Crown Prince was married, waited until the Emperor took the Empress on a journey to see the far reaches of the realm — and no one was ever added to the inner palace.

Well. Someone was added.

Several princes and princesses — all born to the Empress.

But that is a story for another time.

......

Jiang Mi rested briefly, refreshed herself, changed into ordinary palace clothes, and walked through the newly renovated Kūnníng Palace with Official Sun.

Her aunt had been Empress, and she had visited the Kūnníng Palace often as a child, but this version was completely unlike the one in her memory. A bathhouse had been added in the side hall — she had been too occupied the night before to look properly; seeing it now, she noticed the walls were set with luminous pearls, magnificent and opulent.

To the south, a garden had been rebuilt. The crape myrtles were in full bloom at this time of year, great clouds of smoky rose — and among all those flowers, a swing stood very prominently.

Jiang Mi walked over and ran her fingers along the chains. The texture was different from ordinary iron — unusually solid, specially crafted, and from it hung a string of small golden bells.

She sat down on the swing, and the bells rang out in a bright, light cascade.

Qiuyu understood at once that her mistress wanted to swing.

She moved behind her and gave a gentle push.

Jiang Mi held the chains. Her skirts rose and fluttered, and the bells rang on, clear and sweet.

She swung her legs with the arc of the swing, breathing in flowers, and something in her chest loosened.

She could not help calling out: "Qiuyu — push me a little higher."

Xiao Huaiyan walked into the Kūnníng Palace and did not find Jiang Mi in the main hall.

A palace attendant answered cautiously: "Your Majesty — the Empress has gone to the small garden."

Xiao Huaiyan said nothing and walked south.

Before he saw her, he heard her — a light, shallow laugh, like clear water running down from a snowy mountain peak.

He turned a corner and stopped. He stood watching the woman on the swing in silence. He had seen her shy smiles, her dutiful smiles, her resigned smiles — but this one was different. Playful, faintly childlike, the smile of a girl with nothing to worry about, vivid and alive. No elaborately crafted doll could compare to this.

"Qiuyu — push me higher, would you?"

He heard her calling out.

His brow tightened. He walked toward them.

The attendants nearby all knelt when they saw him coming.

Jiang Mi had just swung back and was turning to say something to Qiuyu, when she caught a flash in her peripheral vision — and there was Xiao Huaiyan.

She startled. A pair of large hands closed around the dark chains.

The swing stopped abruptly. She swung forward and bumped into him.

Xiao Huaiyan's hand rested on her shoulder. "If you fall, I will have this thing taken down."

Jiang Mi shook her head quickly. She unclipped the safety chain from across her front and explained: "Your Majesty — I have this chain fastened. I will not fall." The unspoken meaning: please do not under any circumstances dismantle the swing.

Xiao Huaiyan looked at her pale, slender fingertips holding that dark chain, and thought: had he known, he would never have had the thing installed.

He lifted her from the swing and settled her into the crook of his arm. "Was it enjoyable?"

Jiang Mi steadied herself on his shoulder, reading his expression — he did not appear to be angry. She hesitated and nodded. "It was — it was all right."

"Next time I will let you go higher."

She was surprised. She had expected a scolding.

Xiao Huaiyan saw her expression and reached out to flick her lightly. "Not complaining about an aching back now, are you? Not exhausted?"

Jiang Mi lay in his arms and said nothing.

Xiao Huaiyan readjusted his hold and carried her in the direction of the bathhouse.

In the steam and mist, the sounds from the pool rose and fell.

Jiang Mi braced against the side of the pool and caught her breath. A burning body pressed against her from behind. He turned her face and kissed her.

Xiao Huaiyan brushed the hair from Jiang Mi's face, his voice low. "Tangtan — call me Sixth Elder Brother."

Jiang Mi only wanted it to end quickly. She wrapped her arms around his neck, trembling. "Sixth... Elder Brother..."

Her voice was soft and tearful, and Xiao Huaiyan's eyes went very dark.

Only after she had said it did Jiang Mi realize what she had called him.

Xiao Huaiyan was the sixth among the princes. She remembered — in another time, he had asked her to call him that too.

Her fingers were caught in his, and she was pulled tightly into his arms.

"Tangtan..." Xiao Huaiyan said something against her ear.

She was too exhausted to hear it clearly, and slipped into sleep.

A life is long. A promise is not a single sentence — it is the companionship and the making-right of all the years that remain.

Jiang Mi had entered the palace carrying anxiety and unease.

Gradually she found that the palace of this life was entirely unlike the one she had known before.

After An'yang was married off under the Imperial Household Department's arrangements, the Worthy Dowager Consort departed for the travelling palace.

The only masters left in the inner palace were herself, Xiao Huaiyan, and her aunt.

But her aunt told her: in a little while, she intended to go to Wǔtái Mountain to recuperate. The air there was clean and the setting peaceful — it suited her.

That made the inner palace emptier still.

Jiang Mi was reluctant to lose her aunt, but her aunt told her she had been in the palace far too long and wanted to go out and see the world while she still could.

Jiang Mi knew it was her aunt's heart's desire. She could only make the most of the days remaining before her departure and spend as much time with her as possible.

As for Xiao Huaiyan — he came back to the Kūnníng Palace almost every night. On the rare occasions when state affairs ran so late that he feared disturbing her sleep, he would simply stay in the Qiánqīng Palace.

Jiang Mi knew that from time to time there were memorials in court requesting the Emperor to take additional consorts.

But she had heard that a few of the leading voices had had certain household improprieties unearthed by the Embroidered Guard, and dared not raise the matter again.

Jiang Mi found herself not much bothered by any of it. She still had that imperial edict.

At that moment, footsteps sounded behind her. She quickly put the edict back into the rosewood box.

Xiao Huaiyan caught sight of what she had been looking at. He pressed her shoulder with a touch of resignation. "I will not give you cause to use that edict."

His hand rested lightly against her lower abdomen. "When will there be movement here?"

Jiang Mi turned to face him, blinking. "Guess."

She smiled before he did.

chapters.title: After the Wedding, Part One
chapters.content:
Jiang Mi sat in the Ci'ning Palace watching palace maids bustle about packing the Empress Dowager's luggage for Wǔtái Mountain.

She looked at the Empress Dowager with reluctance. "Empress Mother — how long do you mean to stay at Wǔtái Mountain? Can you not stay a little longer with Tangtan?"

The Empress Dowager laughed and took Jiang Mi's hand. "I am reluctant to leave you too. But I have been in this palace far too long, and I want to go out while I still can. Wǔtái Mountain is peaceful — it suits me well for recovery. When you have a child in your belly, I will come back."

At the mention of a child, Jiang Mi's expression went slightly unnatural.

The Empress Dowager asked: "Are your monthly cycles regular these days, Tangtan?"

Jiang Mi hesitated, then nodded. "They have been acceptable."

The Empress Dowager pressed her earnestly: "You must be especially attentive. You are the only person in the Emperor's inner palace right now — you must try to conceive early." The greatest regret of the Empress Dowager's life was having no child of her own, and she regarded this matter with great weight.

The Emperor doted on Tangtan now, and whatever his reasons for not taking additional consorts, there was no guarantee he would not do so eventually. While she was still in sole favour, having a child early would only strengthen her position.

Jiang Mi was quiet and smiled softly at the floor. She understood how much a child meant to her aunt — but her own heart had no certainty. In the last life she had attended the Emperor many times and never once conceived.

The Empress Dowager took this only for shyness. She leaned close and said two or three things in Jiang Mi's ear, and watched with satisfaction as Jiang Mi's ears went red.

The Empress Dowager laughed. "You — stop spending all your time here with me. If the Emperor goes to the Kūnníng Palace and cannot find you, he will be here at the Ci'ning Palace paying his respects again."

Teased into taking her leave, Jiang Mi withdrew.

On the phoenix palanquin going back, Jiang Mi sat thinking about her aunt's words, a small, complicated feeling turning in her chest.

She and Xiao Huaiyan were still finding their way with each other — there was something tentative she could not quite name.

She did not know how ordinary husband and wife behaved. She and Xiao Huaiyan seemed to be testing each other, feeling out the edges of one another.

She was probing how far his tolerance extended. He was probing how much she would accept.

This was a working-in. Compared to the Xiao Huaiyan of the last life — the one who had shown his temper freely — this life's Xiao Huaiyan had put away his willfulness and levity and replaced them with warmth and gentleness.

Jiang Mi sometimes wondered: if the bad temper of the last life had been his true nature, how long could this life's Xiao Huaiyan keep it hidden?

She shifted against the cushions, a low ache at her back, a brief flash of exasperation crossing her brow. She thought of what her aunt had just told her — that for the matter of a child, intimacy should not be too frequent.

Jiang Mi had wanted to find a hole in the ground and disappear. Xiao Huaiyan came to the Kūnníng Palace almost every night. Even on the nights her cycle had come, he had not stayed away — he had not touched her, but he had still crowded onto the same bed.

She did not know if some remark had reached her aunt's ears and prompted the pointed reminder.

The phoenix palanquin stopped at the Kūnníng Palace. Jiang Mi stepped down on Qiuyu's arm.

Chéngzhōng had been waiting at the door and came forward with a smile. "This servant greets Her Highness the Empress."

She told him to rise and asked: "Is there something from the Emperor?"

Chéngzhōng nodded. "Your Highness — His Majesty has summoned several Grand Council ministers to discuss important matters, and will not be coming for the evening meal."

Jiang Mi was curious. "The Grand Council? Is there to be a military campaign?"

Chéngzhōng thought of the Emperor's instructions — if the Empress asked, he was to tell her what could be told.

He said: "When His Majesty suppressed the southern rebellion, it emerged that the conspirators had been in contact with spies from a hostile nation who had infiltrated Great Wei. His Majesty intends to send out troops."

Jiang Mi stilled. In her memory of the last life, in the fifth year of the Yuánxī era, rebels had risen in the south. The hostile nation had seized the opportunity and massed their forces at Yúnzhōu, launching an assault. Xiao Huaiyan had led the campaign himself.

These events were happening again in this life — only earlier. She did not know what Xiao Huaiyan would do this time.

When the evening meal came, the imperial kitchen sent an array of fine dishes.

Jiang Mi watched the palace maids set course after course on the table — sweet-and-sour lotus root, cherry-blossom pork, Biwave soup, crab with double bamboo shoots — all dishes she particularly liked.

Since entering the palace, every meal the imperial kitchen prepared had suited her taste perfectly.

She glanced at Qiuyu standing nearby and said with a smile: "How much has the imperial kitchen given you in favour? Do not let yourself be shortchanged."

Qiuyu looked bewildered. "Your Highness — why would the imperial kitchen give this servant anything?"

Jiang Mi had meant it as a jest, but Qiuyu seemed genuinely puzzled. She asked directly: "Has no one from the imperial kitchen asked you about my preferences?"

Qiuyu shook her head. "No, Your Highness. The imperial kitchen has never asked this servant anything. This servant assumed Your Highness had told them yourself."

Jiang Mi found it odd. Could it all be coincidence? Or perhaps the imperial kitchen had found out her preferences through other channels — those people were sharp enough for it.

After the meal, she walked in the garden a while to aid her digestion, then went back inside when the sky had gone fully dark.

She assumed Xiao Huaiyan would be occupied with military and state affairs tonight and would not come.

Thinking of her aunt's imminent departure for Wǔtái Mountain, she could not help getting out a few travel books to page through.

Of those, the ones written by the author called Sōngxún were the most vivid and full of living detail.

But when she remembered that Sōngxún was Shen Qiānxiū, she set the book aside.

She had read only a few pages before drowsiness took hold, and she fell asleep.

Around midnight, the imperial palanquin arrived at the Kūnníng Palace.

Xiao Huaiyan raised a hand to silence the kneeling palace maids and eunuchs.

He walked into the sleeping chamber. A single lamp had been left burning. The air carried the faint sweet scent that always clung to Jiang Mi. He lifted the hangings and found her deep in sleep.

She lay on her side, one arm resting on top of the quilt, one bare foot — seeking coolness — stretched out from under it, curled slightly. It was rather endearing.

Xiao Huaiyan let his gaze rest on her, and reached out to hold that foot. His fingers moved, involuntarily, and the pressure in his hand slipped out of control a little — startling the sleeping woman.

Jiang Mi frowned and kicked twice. In her dream something like water-weeds had caught her foot and she could not shake free.

Xiao Huaiyan saw her about to wake and reluctantly tucked the foot back under the quilt and straightened the bedding over her.

He was going to the washroom to bathe when he noticed the book by her pillow. He picked it up and set it on the table, where he saw several more travel books — one by someone called Sōngxún, its pages noticeably more worn than the others.

He picked it up, glanced at it, and set it down again.

He came out of the bath, still faintly damp, and lay down beside Jiang Mi. He settled his hand on her waist. She made a small sound.

He had tired her out last night. He had no particular intention now.

He drew her into his arms and closed his eyes.

The next morning Xiao Huaiyan went to court and left without waking her.

Jiang Mi woke and, bowing her head to fasten her inner garments, saw the marks on her chest — and knew Xiao Huaiyan had come back in the night.

In the imperial study, Xiao Huaiyan read the dispatch from Yúnzhōu and composed a reply, which he had Gù Chǎng send on.

Li Fu brought tea. "Your Majesty — do rest a moment."

Xiao Huaiyan put down his vermilion brush, as if remembering something. "Have someone find me a few books by a writer called Sōngxún."

Li Fu thought the name sounded faintly familiar, then it came to him, and he said with eager helpfulness: "Your Majesty, there is no need to search far — this Sōngxún is none other than the new top scholar Your Majesty himself chose, young Master Shen. My, that young Master Shen is truly gifted — he writes so well, he..."

Li Fu choked on the words. That look the Emperor was giving him — why was it so frightening?

chapters.title: After the Wedding, Part Two
chapters.content:
Xiao Huaiyan's fingers tapped the table. His narrow eyes were coldly assessing. His voice came out light and ice-edged. "Is that so."

Li Fu felt as though the Emperor's eyes were tempered with frozen water. The question sent every hair on his body upright, and a cold sweat began to seep down his back.

This particular version of the Emperor — when had it last been seen?

Since the imperial wedding, the Emperor had been in remarkably good humour — spring-warm and easy, like sunshine on new growth. The attendants below all felt themselves basking in it. In court he had listened to his ministers' reports with more patience than before; everyone could see the Emperor's mood was excellent, and even difficult matters delivered plainly would not be punished too harshly.

Li Fu dared not reply. He felt a cold unease.

Xiao Huaiyan was silent for a moment. "Since you speak so highly of them — find a few copies."

Even Li Fu at his most obtuse could tell he had said something wrong. He could not imagine what this young Master Shen had done to strike the Emperor's reverse scale. He dared not dawdle and went immediately to carry out the order.

Before long, Li Fu had gathered several of the books and presented them at the imperial desk.

Xiao Huaiyan looked at the pale green covers — identical to the one he had seen in the Kūnníng Palace, except that one had been new and the one by Jiang Mi's bed had been worn with use.

He had only glanced at it briefly before and paid it no mind.

Xiao Huaiyan leafed through the books and looked at what was written inside. The corner of his mouth pulled slightly. "Nothing so remarkable."

Li Fu standing nearby dared not venture an opinion. Whatever the Emperor said was correct.

Xiao Huaiyan closed the books and instructed Li Fu: "Go and find the manuscripts I wrote during my study travels."

Li Fu quickly said: "Yes, Your Majesty."

......

Jiang Mi rose, changed into a red crossed-collar dress embroidered with gold dragon-and-phoenix patterns, and chose a five-phoenix gold hair ornament newly delivered by the Garment Bureau. She took Official Sun's hand and went to the main hall to meet with the heads of each palace office.

Her aunt was leaving for Wǔtái Mountain, and the palace affairs were gradually being transferred to her hands. With so few mistresses in the palace at present, every office had been fairly idle.

Jiang Mi turned through the register and listened to the reports from those below.

She considered for a moment and said: "It seems to this Palace that some of the palace maids have grown older. We might release a batch — those who have reached twenty-five years of age — and allow them to leave the palace to marry as they choose."

The office heads exchanged a look. They had not expected the Empress to issue a benevolent decree so soon after entering the palace. For some palace maids, this was good news; for others, it was not — some had family waiting outside and would be glad, while others had no one in the outside world and would have to find their own way. But none of them dared raise an objection on the first matter the Empress had decided herself. They all bowed together. "This servant respectfully obeys Her Highness's decree."

Jiang Mi sent them back to compile the names into a register and to inform the Imperial Household Department as well.

She reminded herself to mention this to Xiao Huaiyan.

Before long, the Imperial Household Department delivered some fresh lychees.

Qiuyu selected the best ones, peeled them and had them chilled on ice, and brought them over. "Your Highness — do try these lychees. They came from Guǎngzhōu by fast horses, all the way to the capital. I just lifted the cloth on top and everything inside is still deliciously cold."

Jiang Mi took one of the ice-chilled lychees and raised a silver fork to put the pearly fruit in her mouth — then stopped.

She remembered what her aunt had said: her constitution was best kept away from things that were too cold.

Jiang Mi hesitated and set the fruit back down. She said to Qiuyu: "Take those chilled ones away for the others to share. Have the imperial kitchen make me a warm lychee compote instead."

Qiuyu nodded and thanked her happily for the treat. She could not help feeling a little puzzled — back at the marquessate, whenever lychee season came, her mistress had always insisted on having them iced.

Jiang Mi ate half a bowl of warm lychee compote and noticed, as she glanced at the time, that there had been no summons from the Qiánqīng Palace — Xiao Huaiyan would not be coming for the midday meal.

After eating, she sat at the table to read through the palace affairs register her aunt had handed over to her. She noticed the travel books nearby and tidied them a little, and realised the Sōngxún volume that had been sitting there was gone.

She wondered if Official Sun or Qiuyu had put it away.

She did not give it much thought and picked up a brush to mark the important passages in her aunt's register.

She had barely started when she heard the sounds of greeting from outside. She was puzzled — why was he here at this hour?

She had just risen when she saw Xiao Huaiyan come around the screen.

Before she could bow, Xiao Huaiyan caught her and said warmly: "How many times have I said there is no need for ceremony."

Jiang Mi naturally answered agreeably — and would go on doing the right things regardless.

Xiao Huaiyan asked in an offhand manner: "What were you doing?"

"Just reading." She could not very well say she was reading the palace affairs register in front of him.

He asked, his eyes warm: "Which book? Let me have a look."

Jiang Mi glanced at him and offered a small smile. "These idle books are hardly fit for the Emperor's attention. Is Your Majesty not busy today?" She remembered Chéngzhōng saying the previous evening that he was to send out troops against the hostile nation — why was he here in the middle of the day instead of in the imperial study?

Xiao Huaiyan saw her evading and deflecting and felt something difficult settle in him.

The image of Jiang Mi and Shen Qiānxiū at the prayer tree at the Qiānshuāng Temple — hanging the red wish-ribbon together — flickered across his mind.

His eyes darkened. A strange emotion surged and churned, leaving his heart sour and bitter.

Was she still thinking of Shen Qiānxiū?

Did she prefer him to stay busy with state affairs in the imperial study and leave her alone?

Jiang Mi saw that Xiao Huaiyan had gone quiet for a long time and his expression had gone odd. She could not think of anything she had said wrong. What was the matter with him?

In the midst of her puzzled look, Xiao Huaiyan spoke. "Busy — but the head-sickness came on, so I came back first. Tangtan — come and press it for me."

He took her hand and drew her toward the day-couch.

Jiang Mi went along easily enough. She had imagined he would sit and she would stand to press his temples.

But Xiao Huaiyan had her sit on the couch while he lay down with his head in her lap.

In the middle of the day, this intimate arrangement made Jiang Mi slightly self-conscious.

His burning breath pressed close against her, and when he shifted even slightly she could feel it. But she watched his eyes close, his brow knitted together, and he looked genuinely unwell. She raised her hand and placed it at his temple and began to press.

The scene brought something back to her — Xiao Huaiyan drunk and in pain, and her aunt sending her to press his head for him. That time Xiao Huaiyan had lain silent through it, and then for some reason had suddenly caught her wrist and seemed to lightly run his thumb across the red birthmark on the inside of her wrist.

Jiang Mi's hands kept their rhythm. "Is this pressure all right, Your Majesty?"

His voice reached him soft and low. Xiao Huaiyan's thoughts stirred. His hand settled on her waist. "It is. Very good."

Jiang Mi felt his hand beginning to wander. She said helplessly: "Your Majesty — how long have you had this head-sickness? Has a physician been to look at it?"

After a moment Xiao Huaiyan replied: "It is an old complaint. I have had it since childhood."

Jiang Mi's hands paused. She tried to remember — had the Xiao Huaiyan of the last life had this? She could not recall.

Xiao Huaiyan added: "It is nothing serious — just occasional bouts. Are you getting tired?"

She was still quite all right. She was about to say so when he spoke again: "Tangtan — if you are tired, read to me instead. Your voice is pleasant — it would ease and settle me."

Odd as the request was, Jiang Mi found it harmless enough. Some people wanted music for their headaches; Xiao Huaiyan apparently wanted to be read to.

"What shall I read, Your Majesty?"

Xiao Huaiyan gave a low clearing cough and drew a booklet from his sleeve. He said in an unhurried tone: "This one will do."

Jiang Mi took it and opened it. Her eyes widened in surprise — this was Xiao Huaiyan's own handwriting. And it appeared to be a manuscript.

Leafing through it quickly, she saw it seemed to be an account of what he had seen and experienced during his study travels, with his own annotations throughout.

She glanced at him, then parted her lips and began to read aloud.

As she read, Xiao Huaiyan found himself absorbed.

Her voice ran somewhat sweet, while the writing was occasionally sharp-edged — hearing it come out of her mouth produced a strange effect that only intensified his desire to possess all of her.

To have everything she thought about be him.

He very much wanted to press Jiang Mi down and demand: do you have me in your heart? Even a sliver of feeling?

But he had never dared to ask.
